question: Compared to the metals being joined, the melting point of solder is ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __lower**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Solder__ is a fusible metal alloy used to create a permanent bond between metal workpieces.
 
• The melting point of solder is lower than that of the metals being joined.
 
• This allows the solder to melt and flow into the joint without damaging the base metals.
 
• Solders are typically made of tin-lead alloy, though lead-free options are also common.
 
• By having a lower melting point, soldering ensures effective bonding without affecting the structural integrity of the metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Applications of Solder:**

 
 
• Solder is widely used in electronics manufacturing to connect components to circuit boards.
 
• It is also used in plumbing to join pipes and fittings.
 
• Jewelry-making and metalwork also utilize solder for precision bonding.
 
 
 
• **Types of Solder:**
 
 
• Lead-based solder: Comprises tin and lead, offering easy flow and low melting points.
 
• Lead-free solder: Environmentally friendly, made of tin mixed with other metals like silver or copper.
